# Archi Rent — full site content (English)


## Car Rental in Georgia — Archi Rent | Prices, Fleet, Terms
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/



### In short — what we offer

Archi Rent is a car rental company that has been operating in Georgia since 2019. The fleet holds more than 120 vehicles, from economy class through off-road 4x4s to eight-seat minivans. We rent to tourists as well as to local companies on long-term corporate contracts.

Minimum age: 21 years
Driving experience: 2+ years
Deposit: 300–1500 ₾
Mileage: Unlimited
Fuel policy: Full → full
Insurance: CDW included

### Vehicle categories and prices

Below are the base daily rates for rentals of 1–6 days. From 7 days a 10% discount applies, from 30 days — 25%. The full table and the cost of extras are on the pricing page.

Category | Example | 1–6 days | 7–29 days | 30+ days | Deposit
Economy class | Toyota Prius, Hyundai Elantra | 75 ₾ | 68 ₾ | 56 ₾ | 300 ₾
Crossover / SUV | Toyota RAV4, Hyundai Tucson | 130 ₾ | 117 ₾ | 98 ₾ | 600 ₾
Business class | Toyota Camry, Mercedes E-Class | 210 ₾ | 189 ₾ | 158 ₾ | 1000 ₾
Off-road 4x4 | Land Cruiser Prado, Delica | 240 ₾ | 216 ₾ | 180 ₾ | 1200 ₾
Minivan, 7–8 seats | Toyota Alphard, Hyundai Staria | 200 ₾ | 180 ₾ | 150 ₾ | 1000 ₾
Commercial van | Ford Transit, Mercedes Sprinter | 185 ₾ | 167 ₾ | 139 ₾ | 800 ₾

Included in the price: CDW insurance coverage, unlimited mileage within Georgia, servicing, 24/7 roadside assistance, winter tyres in season and VAT. Not included: fuel, traffic fines, additional drivers and cross-border permits.

### Where you can pick up your car

- Tbilisi International Airport (TBS): Meet and greet in the arrivals hall, 24 hours a day. Delivery is free from 3 days. Delivery 0 ₾ (3+ days) / 40 ₾ (1–2 days) Night handover and return available
- Kutaisi Airport (KUT): The main hub for low-cost flights — we meet you according to your flight time. Delivery 0 ₾ (5+ days) / 60 ₾ Return in Batumi or Tbilisi possible
- Batumi Airport (BUS): An expanded summer-season fleet right on the Black Sea coast. Delivery 0 ₾ (5+ days) / 50 ₾ One-way rental — from 100 ₾
- Tbilisi, Vazha-Pshavela Avenue: Head office and service centre. Inspect the car on site. Mon–Sun 09:00–21:00 Delivery within the city is free
- Batumi, Kutaisi, Telavi — city centre: Delivery to your address by prior arrangement. Delivery 30–80 ₾ depending on the city
- Border crossings (Sarpi, Kazbegi): By individual arrangement, for rentals of at least 5 days. Delivery from 120 ₾

### Who rents a car in Georgia

- Tourists — Georgia's main routes (Kazbegi, Svaneti, Kakheti, Vardzia) are hard to reach by public transport; a car cuts travel time by two to three times.
- Business travellers — on a short visit a business-class car works out cheaper than taxis from day three onwards.
- Companies — long-term corporate rental is an alternative to buying a fleet: no capital tied up, no maintenance administration to run.
- Local residents — while their own car is in the workshop, for seasonal needs or for a family trip.

### What sets us apart

- Transparent pricing: The rate shown on the website is final. No hidden commissions, no "service fees" and no compulsory extra insurance. 
- Average fleet age — 4 years: Every vehicle is serviced every 8,000 km, and the full history is logged digitally. 
- Deposit blocked, not charged: The amount is blocked on your card and released within 3 business days of returning the car. 
- Roadside assistance nationwide: A 24/7 hotline; in the event of a breakdown a replacement car reaches you within 6 hours. 
- Our own software: We run the fleet on our own system, FleetFreak — which is why we know exactly which car frees up when, and double bookings are impossible. 
- Service in three languages: Georgian, English and Russian — including the rental agreement. 

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How much does it cost to rent a car in Georgia per day?
A: An economy-class car starts at 75 GEL (roughly 28 USD) per day, a crossover at 130 GEL and an off-road 4x4 at 240 GEL. For rentals over 7 days the price drops by 10%, and from 30 days by 25%.
Q: What documents do I need to rent a car?
A: An ID card or passport, a driving licence held for at least 2 years, and a credit or debit card for the deposit. Foreign nationals need an international driving permit only if their national licence is not issued in the Latin alphabet.
Q: Can I cross the border in a rental car?
A: Travel to Armenia is allowed with a permit arranged in advance — 150 GEL, plus international insurance. Travel to Turkey is possible for selected categories. Travel to Azerbaijan and Russia is prohibited.
Q: Is the mileage limited?
A: No. Mileage within Georgia is unlimited on every rate. For cross-border trips a daily limit of 300 km applies.
Q: What happens in the event of an accident?
A: The CDW insurance included in the price covers damage above the excess (300–1,200 GEL depending on category). The excess can be waived entirely for an extra 25–45 GEL per day.
Q: Can I return the car in a different city?
A: Yes. One-way rentals on the Tbilisi↔Kutaisi↔Batumi routes start at 100 GEL; other cities by arrangement.

More questions and answers are on the FAQ page.

### FleetFreak — our fleet management system

We run the Archi Rent fleet on our own app, FleetFreak. The same system is available to other rental companies: bookings, conflict detection, daily P&L, per-vehicle ROI and payback period, expenses, loans and insurance all in one place. Details are on the FleetFreak page.

This site is informational — we have no online payment system. To book a car, call us or send an email; during business hours you will hear back within 15 minutes.

The fleet holds more than 120 vehicles across six categories, with an average age of 4 years. Below are the typical models, specifications and daily rates for each category.

### Economy class — from 75 ₾ per day

Our most popular category. Ideal for getting around the city and for trips on paved roads: Tbilisi–Kakheti, Tbilisi–Batumi, Tbilisi–Borjomi. The hybrid models save a great deal of fuel — the Tbilisi–Batumi run (370 km) costs roughly 55 GEL in fuel.

- Toyota Prius (hybrid): 2018–2022 · 1.8 hybrid · automatic, 75 GEL/day
- Hyundai Elantra: 2019–2023 · 1.6 petrol · automatic, 82 GEL/day
- Toyota Corolla: 2020–2023 · 1.6 petrol · automatic, 88 GEL/day

### Crossovers and SUVs — from 130 ₾ per day

The best choice for travelling through Georgia's regions. The higher ground clearance lets you take the mountain roads of Kazbegi, Racha and Kakheti safely. For Svaneti and Tusheti we recommend the off-road 4x4 category.

- Toyota RAV4: 2019–2023 · 2.5 hybrid / 2.0 petrol · AWD, 145 GEL/day
- Hyundai Tucson: 2020–2023 · 2.0 petrol · AWD, 130 GEL/day
- Mitsubishi Outlander: 2018–2022 · 2.4 petrol · 4WD, 138 GEL/day

### Business class — from 210 ₾ per day

Executive cars for business visits, conferences and transfers. Available with a driver if required — an extra 120 GEL per day (8 hours).

- Toyota Camry: 2020–2023 · 2.5 hybrid · automatic, 210 GEL/day
- Mercedes-Benz E-Class: 2019–2022 · 2.0 diesel · automatic, 290 GEL/day
- BMW 5 Series: 2019–2022 · 2.0 petrol · automatic, 310 GEL/day

### Off-road 4x4 — from 240 ₾ per day

The only category cleared for the gravel roads of Svaneti (Ushguli), Tusheti (the Abano Pass), Khevsureti and Tbeti. These vehicles come with a locking differential or low-range gearing.

- Toyota Land Cruiser Prado: 2017–2022 · 2.8 diesel · 4WD, 330 GEL/day
- Mitsubishi Delica D:5: 2016–2021 · 2.2 diesel · 4WD, 290 GEL/day
- Mitsubishi Pajero: 2015–2020 · 3.0 petrol · 4WD, 240 GEL/day

### Minivans and minibuses — from 200 ₾ per day

For family trips and small groups. Seven to eight seats, a large boot and room for up to three child seats.

- Toyota Alphard: 2018–2022 · 2.5 hybrid · automatic, 310 GEL/day
- Hyundai Staria: 2021–2024 · 2.2 diesel · automatic, 260 GEL/day
- Mercedes-Benz Vito: 2018–2022 · 2.1 diesel · automatic, 200 GEL/day

### Commercial vans — from 185 ₾ per day

For construction, retail and logistics companies. Available on monthly and annual corporate contracts, with branding permitted.

- Ford Transit: 2019–2023 · 2.0 diesel · manual, 185 GEL/day
- Mercedes-Benz Sprinter: 2018–2022 · 2.1 diesel · manual, 215 GEL/day

### How we maintain the fleet

- Servicing every 8,000 km or every 6 months, whichever comes first.
- Winter tyres from 1 December to 1 April on every vehicle, at no charge.
- A full visual inspection and photo record before every rental.
- Wet cleaning of the interior after every customer.
- Average fleet age — 4 years; vehicles older than 8 years leave the fleet.

Availability of a specific model varies by date. At the time of booking we confirm the category; a specific model is guaranteed only by prior arrangement.

Call us and we will check availability for your dates.

The deposit is blocked on a credit or debit card when the rental starts and is released within 3 business days of the car being returned, provided there is no damage or fine. When paying in cash, the deposit is taken in cash and returned on the spot.

Contracts longer than 3 months and covering 3 or more vehicles are priced individually. Corporate clients receive:

## Rental terms — documents, age, deposit | Archi Rent
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/terms/

Below are the full terms, which form an integral part of the rental agreement. The agreement is drawn up in Georgian, English or Russian.

### Required documents

Category | Identity | Driving licence | Additional
Georgian citizen | ID card | National, held 2+ years | Card for the deposit
Foreign national (Latin alphabet) | Passport | National licence | Card for the deposit
Foreign national (non-Latin) | Passport | National + IDP | Card for the deposit
Company | Extract from the register | Driver's licence | Power of attorney, company stamp

An IDP (International Driving Permit) is required if your national licence is not issued in the Latin alphabet — for example an Arabic, Chinese, Japanese or Georgian licence used abroad. Licences from the EU, the USA, the United Kingdom and CIS countries are valid in Georgia as they are.

### Age and driving experience

Category | Minimum age | Minimum experience | Young driver surcharge
Economy class | 21 years | 2 years | —
Crossover / SUV | 23 years | 3 years | 15 ₾ / day (ages 23–25)
Business class | 25 years | 5 years | 25 ₾ / day (ages 25–27)
Off-road 4x4 | 25 years | 4 years | 25 ₾ / day (ages 25–27)
Minivan | 23 years | 3 years | 15 ₾ / day (ages 23–25)
Commercial van | 25 years | 3 years | —

There is no upper age limit.

### Fuel policy

- We apply the "full to full" principle: the car is handed over with a full tank and must be returned with a full tank.
- If the tank is not full, we charge the cost of the fuel plus a 20 ₾ service fee.
- Misfuelling (diesel in a petrol car or vice versa) is not covered by the insurance — the renter bears the cost.
- Hybrid vehicles run on petrol alone; they do not need to be plugged in.

### Insurance and liability

The price includes CDW (Collision Damage Waiver) and TPL (third-party liability). CDW caps the renter's liability at the excess amount — see the pricing page. Adding SCDW reduces the excess to zero.

#### The insurance does not cover

- Driving under the influence of alcohol, narcotics or psychotropic substances
- Driving by a person not named as a driver in the rental agreement
- Damage sustained on gravel or unpaved roads unless the vehicle is in the 4x4 category
- Damage to tyres, wheels, the underbody and the interior
- Loss of the keys (400–1,200 ₾ depending on the model)
- Use of the vehicle as a taxi, for haulage or for any other commercial purpose without prior written consent

### Cross-border travel

Country | Status | Cost | Daily limit
Armenia | Permitted | 150 ₾ | 300 km
Turkey | Permitted (selected categories) | 250 ₾ | 300 km
Azerbaijan | Prohibited | — | —
Russia | Prohibited | — | —

Cross-border permission must be arranged at least 48 hours in advance — an international insurance policy and a power of attorney have to be prepared. Crossing the border without permission is a breach of the agreement and results in forfeiture of the entire deposit.

### Booking, cancellation and changes

- Bookings are confirmed by phone or email; no prepayment is required.
- Cancellation more than 48 hours ahead — free of charge.
- Cancellation 24–48 hours ahead — one day's rate is charged.
- Cancellation less than 24 hours ahead, or a no-show — two days' rate is charged.
- Changing the dates is free if the car is available on the new dates.
- Early return — unused days are refunded, recalculated at the rate applicable to the actual rental length.

### The renter's obligations

- Use the vehicle only for the purpose set out in the rental agreement.
- Observe the traffic regulations; all fines are at the renter's expense.
- In the event of an accident, call 112 and our hotline immediately, and do not leave the scene until the report has been drawn up.
- Leave the vehicle locked; never leave the documents inside the car.
- Stop driving and contact us as soon as a technical fault appears.
- Return the vehicle in the same condition, allowing for normal wear and tear.

### Penalties and additional charges

Breach | Charge
Smoking inside the car | 150 ₾
Transporting an animal without a proper carrier | 100 ₾
Returning the car with a dirty interior | 30–80 ₾
Tank not returned full | Cost of fuel + 20 ₾
Late return of more than 2 hours | 1/3 of the daily rate per 3 hours
Processing a traffic fine | Amount of the fine + 20 ₾
Loss of the keys | 400–1 200 ₾
Loss of the documents | 200 ₾

This page is informational and does not constitute a public offer. Only the signed rental agreement is legally binding. The terms may change — the date of the latest revision is shown at the foot of the page.

We will email you a sample rental agreement as soon as you ask.


## Frequently asked questions about car rental | Archi Rent
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/faq/

Answers to the questions our customers ask most often. If yours is not on the list, just give us a call.

### Prices and payment

Q: How much does it cost to rent a car in Georgia for one day?
A: An economy-class car starts at 75 GEL (≈28 USD), a crossover at 130 GEL (≈48 USD) and an off-road 4x4 at 240 GEL (≈89 USD). For rentals of 1–2 days the rate is slightly higher.
Q: Is there a discount for long-term rentals?
A: Yes. From 7 days the price falls by 10%, and from 30 days by 25%. On corporate contracts longer than 3 months the discount reaches 40%.
Q: Can I pay online through the website?
A: No. This site is informational and has no online payment module. Payment is made on the spot in cash or by card, or in advance by bank transfer for companies.
Q: Which currency do you settle in?
A: The main currency is the lari. In cash we also accept US dollars and euros at the National Bank rate on the day of payment.
Q: Are there any hidden charges?
A: No. The rate shown on the site includes VAT, CDW insurance, servicing and unlimited mileage. The only additional charges are for the extras you choose yourself.
Q: Do prices go up in high season?
A: Yes, a seasonal coefficient of +15% applies in July and August. During the Easter and New Year weeks it is +10%.

### Documents and requirements

Q: What documents do I need?
A: A passport or ID card, a driving licence held for at least 2 years, and a card for the deposit. Companies additionally need an extract from the register and a power of attorney.
Q: Do I need an International Driving Permit (IDP)?
A: Only if your national licence is not issued in the Latin alphabet. Licences from the EU, the USA, the United Kingdom, Israel and the CIS countries are valid in Georgia as they are.
Q: What is the minimum age to rent a car?
A: Economy class from 21 with 2 years' experience. Crossovers and minivans from 23. Business class and 4x4 from 25. Drivers under 27 pay a young driver surcharge of 15–25 GEL per day.
Q: Can I add a second driver?
A: Yes, for 20 GEL per day, up to two additional drivers. Each must meet the same age and experience requirements and sign the rental agreement.

### Deposit and insurance

Q: How large is the deposit and when is it returned?
A: From 300 GEL (economy class) up to 1,200 GEL (4x4). The amount is blocked on the card rather than charged, and is released within 3 business days of the car being returned.
Q: What happens if I damage the car?
A: CDW insurance covers damage above the excess. The excess is 300 GEL on economy class and 1,200 GEL on a 4x4. Adding SCDW (25–45 GEL per day) reduces the excess to zero.
Q: Are tyres and wheels covered by the insurance?
A: No. Tyres, wheels, the underbody, the mirrors and the interior are not covered by standard CDW. Replacing a tyre costs 120–400 GEL.
Q: Who pays traffic fines?
A: The renter. A fine can arrive up to 30 days after the rental; in that case we charge the amount of the fine plus 20 GEL for processing.

### Driving and routes

Q: Can I drive to Svaneti (Mestia, Ushguli)?
A: The road as far as Mestia is paved and any category will do. The stretch to Ushguli is gravel — only the off-road 4x4 category is permitted there. Damage sustained in any other category is not covered by insurance.
Q: Is it possible to drive to Tusheti (Omalo)?
A: The Abano Pass is open roughly from June to October and requires an off-road 4x4. Prior written agreement is needed, and an additional excess of 500 GEL applies on this route.
Q: What are the roads like in winter?
A: The main highways (Tbilisi–Batumi, Tbilisi–Kazbegi) stay open all year, although the Gudauri section closes from time to time because of avalanche risk. From 1 December to 1 April every vehicle is fitted with winter tyres.
Q: Is the mileage limited?
A: Within Georgia, no — mileage is unlimited. For cross-border trips a daily limit of 300 km applies, with each extra kilometre charged at 0.5 GEL.
Q: Where can I find a charger for an electric car?
A: We currently have no electric cars in the fleet — only hybrids, which never need charging. A hybrid runs on ordinary petrol.

### Pickup and return

Q: Can I pick the car up at the airport?
A: Yes, at Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Batumi airports. In Tbilisi delivery is free from 3 days, and in Kutaisi and Batumi from 5 days. For shorter rentals the charge is 40–60 GEL.
Q: Is night-time pickup possible?
A: Yes, 24 hours a day. Between 22:00 and 07:00 an extra 40 GEL is charged.
Q: Can I return the car in another city?
A: Yes. One-way rentals on the Tbilisi↔Kutaisi↔Batumi routes start at 100 GEL. Other cities by arrangement.
Q: What happens if I return the car late?
A: Up to 2 hours late is free. After that we charge one third of the daily rate for every 3 hours started; a delay of more than 8 hours counts as a full extra day.
Q: How does the handover and return work?
A: We complete a handover report with photo documentation: we photograph all four sides of the car, the interior, the odometer and the fuel level. The same procedure is repeated on return — which rules out any dispute over damage.

### Other questions

Q: Can I use the car as a taxi or on Bolt?
A: No. Commercial use (taxi, courier work, haulage) is prohibited without prior written consent and voids the insurance coverage.
Q: Can I travel with a pet?
A: Yes, in a proper carrier or with a seat protector. Carrying an animal without a carrier incurs a 100 GEL charge for the extra cleaning.
Q: Can I rent a car with a driver?
A: Yes. The chauffeur service costs 120 GEL per day (8 hours), with overtime at 20 GEL per hour. It is available for business class, minivans and 4x4s.
Q: Do you provide child seats?
A: Yes, in three age groups (0–3, 3–7 and 7–12 years) at 10 GEL per day. Georgian law requires children under 12 to travel in a proper child seat.
Q: What should I do if the car breaks down on the road?
A: Call our hotline — roadside assistance operates 24/7. If the fault is technical and not caused by the renter, we will deliver a replacement car within 6 hours at no charge.
Q: Do you offer leasing or instalment plans?
A: Long-term operating rental (12–36 months) is available to companies. It is not leasing — the vehicle stays on our balance sheet and servicing is at our expense.

Call or email us — during business hours you will hear back within 15 minutes.

## About us — Archi Rent, car rental in Georgia since 2019
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/about/

Archi Rent has been renting out cars since 2019. We started with 8 cars in Tbilisi — today the fleet holds more than 120 vehicles and we operate from six locations.

### By the numbers

Founded: 2019
Vehicles in the fleet: 120+
Locations: 6
Rentals per year: 4,800+
Average fleet age: 4 years
Employees: 34

### How we work

Our model is simple: we own the fleet outright, we service it in our own workshop, and we retire a car from the fleet before repair costs turn it into a loss-maker. That gives us two advantages: predictable prices for the customer and a predictable margin for us.

- Fleet renewal — a car leaves the fleet at 8 years or 200,000 km, whichever comes first.
- Servicing — our own service centre in Tbilisi, every 8,000 km.
- Pricing — one transparent rate; all extras are optional.
- Accounting — revenue, costs and returns are tracked separately for every vehicle.

### Fleet economics

The decisive metric in the rental business is utilisation — the share of the year a vehicle actually spends on rent. Our target is 65% annually; in the summer season it reaches 85% and in winter it falls to around 45%. ROI, ROA and payback period are calculated automatically for every vehicle in our own system, FleetFreak.

Metric | Economy class | Crossover | 4x4
Purchase price | 38 000 ₾ | 78 000 ₾ | 125 000 ₾
Average utilisation | 70% | 65% | 55%
Annual revenue | 19 200 ₾ | 30 800 ₾ | 48 200 ₾
Annual costs (servicing, insurance) | 5 400 ₾ | 8 900 ₾ | 14 600 ₾
Payback period | ~33 months | ~43 months | ~45 months

The table is indicative and illustrates a model rather than actual financial statements. Its purpose is to show how unit economics are calculated in the rental business.

### Our principles

- A price that doesn't change at the counter: What you see on the site is what you pay. We will not offer you "compulsory extra insurance" at handover. 
- Photo records from both sides: At handover and return we photograph the car from all four sides. Disputes over damage are impossible, because both parties hold the evidence. 
- A replacement car within 6 hours: If the car fails through our fault, we will deliver a replacement free of charge anywhere in the country. 
- Documentation in three languages: The rental agreement is available in Georgian, English and Russian — you sign what you can actually read. 

### Corporate clients

We work with construction, logistics and consulting companies. A corporate contract covers a fixed monthly rate, a replacement vehicle, servicing and a single invoice. For a company this is an alternative to running its own fleet without tying up capital.

Email us for a corporate offer — we will prepare a quote based on your volume.

## FleetFreak — fleet management software for car rental businesses
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/fleet-management-software/

FleetFreak is the app we use ourselves to run a 120-vehicle fleet. The same system is available to other rental companies — from a small five-car operation up to a few hundred vehicles.

### The problem it solves

Small and mid-sized rental businesses usually run on Excel and notes on a phone. That produces three familiar problems: double bookings, unrecorded expenses, and no idea which vehicle is paying for itself and which is not. FleetFreak closes all three in a single database.

- Double bookings: The system automatically checks for conflicts between bookings, active rentals and maintenance windows — before the booking is even saved. 
- Lost expenses: Expenses are recorded by category and attached to a vehicle. Loan repayments and insurance premiums are projected forward automatically. 
- Unknown profitability: ROI, ROA, payback period and utilisation rate are calculated separately for every vehicle — so you can see which car should be sold. 

### Core features

Area | What it does
Fleet | Vehicle database, maintenance windows, photos, documents
Bookings | Booking, cancellation, converting a booking into a rental, conflict detection
Rentals | Start, extension, early termination, reactivation, historical records
Finance | Daily P&L, revenue and costs across the period, net profit
Investment | ROI, ROA, payback period and utilisation per vehicle and per fleet
Customers | Database, ratings, rental history, statistics
Expenses | Categories, loans, insurance policies, forecasting
Photo records | Vehicle, rental and booking photos in one database
Export | Excel export, JSON backup, automatic backup by email

### How profitability is calculated

Revenue is recognised across the rental period rather than on the day of payment — which gives you a realistic daily P&L. Fines are not counted as revenue. Loan and insurance costs are projected only into future days, so that actual figures for past periods are never distorted.

- ROI = (net rental revenue − costs) ÷ vehicle purchase price
- ROA = net result for the vehicle ÷ current book value of the vehicle
- Payback period = purchase price ÷ average monthly net result
- Utilisation = days spent on rent ÷ calendar days in the period

### Technical details

Platform: Android 7.0+ / iOS 13+
Technology: Flutter
Database: SQLite (local)
Internet: Not required
Interface languages: Georgian, English
Current version: 2.16

Data is stored on the device — nothing is sent to an external server automatically. Backups are written as a JSON file and, if you wish, emailed to you automatically on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule.

### Who it is for

- Rental companies with 5 to 300 vehicles
- Fleet owners who place their vehicles with partner companies
- Tour operators running their own vehicles
- Leasing and operating-rental companies

### Frequently asked questions about the software

Q: How much does FleetFreak cost?
A: The basic version is free. Advanced features (multi-user mode, centralised synchronisation, integrations) are priced individually according to the size of your fleet.
Q: Does it work without an internet connection?
A: Yes. The database is local, so the app works fully offline. An internet connection is needed only to email a backup.
Q: Can I migrate my data from Excel?
A: Yes. Vehicles, customers and historical rentals can be imported from a structured file. We help with the migration.
Q: How many users does it support?
A: The basic version is designed for a single device. Multi-user mode is part of the advanced version.
Q: Do you get access to my data?
A: No. The database sits on your device and backups go only to the email address you specify yourself.

Tell us the size of your fleet and we will send you a demo version and a rollout plan.

### Toyota Prius (hybrid)
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/fleet/toyota-prius/
Category: Economy class | Years: 2018–2022 | Engine: 1.8 hybrid | automatic | fwd | 5 seats | 4.5 l/100km | clearance 145 mm

The Prius is the car most of our customers end up choosing for a first trip around Georgia, and the reason is simple: fuel. In mixed driving the hybrid drivetrain sits at around 4.5 l/100 km, which turns the Tbilisi–Batumi run (370 km) into roughly 55 ₾ of petrol, and city traffic costs almost nothing because the electric motor does most of the work at low speed.

It is a five-seat hatchback with room for two large suitcases, so a couple or a family of three travels comfortably; four adults with luggage will feel tight. Ground clearance is 145 mm — fine for asphalt routes such as Kakheti, Borjomi, Kutaisi and the highway towards Kazbegi, but not for gravel. The unpaved sections to Ushguli in Svaneti and Omalo in Tusheti are open only to the off-road 4x4 category, and damage taken there in a front-wheel-drive car is not covered by insurance.

At 75 ₾ a day this is also the cheapest way to keep a car for a whole week — the weekly rate is on Prices.

## Articles

### 7 best road-trip routes in Georgia by car
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/blog/avtomobilit-mogzauroba-saqartveloshi/ (2026-06-11)
## Why a car changes the arithmetic

Georgia is a compact country: from Tbilisi you can reach any major region within a day. The difficulty is never the highway — it is the last 5 to 20 km, where the monastery, the fortress or the wine cellar sits and no public transport goes. That detour is exactly what a car buys you, and it is why the same week yields two or three times more stops.

Mileage inside Georgia is unlimited on every one of our rates, so a 400 km day costs no more than a 40 km day. Fuel is the renter's expense under a full-to-full policy.

## All seven routes at a glance

| Route | Distance (one way) | Driving time | Category | Surface | Best season |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tbilisi – Kazbegi | 155 km | 3 h | Crossover, 130 ₾ | Asphalt | May–October |
| Kakheti wine loop | 250 km (loop) | 5–6 h | Economy, 75 ₾ | Asphalt | September–October |
| Tbilisi – Batumi | 370 km | 5 h | Business, 210 ₾ | Motorway | All year |
| Tbilisi – Mestia | 470 km | 8–9 h | Crossover / 4x4 | Asphalt (gravel to Ushguli) | June–September |
| Borjomi – Bakuriani – Vardzia | 290 km (loop) | 6 h | Crossover, 130 ₾ | Asphalt, rough at the end | All year |
| Tbilisi – Ambrolauri (Racha) | 330 km | 6 h | Crossover, 130 ₾ | Narrow asphalt | June–October |
| Pshaveli – Omalo (Tusheti) | 70 km | 4–5 h | Off-road 4x4, 240 ₾ | Gravel | June–October |

### 1. Tbilisi – Kazbegi (Stepantsminda)

The Georgian Military Road past Ananuri, the Zhinvali reservoir and Gudauri. 155 km and three hours without stops — realistically a full day with them. The asphalt is good the whole way, but the switchbacks above Gudauri reward an experienced driver. Tip: the last dependable petrol station is in Pasanauri; beyond Gudauri your options thin out fast. The final 6 km up to Gergeti Trinity Church is a steep dirt track — a crossover manages it dry, but after rain it is a 4x4 job only.

### 2. The Kakheti wine loop

Tbilisi – Signagi – Tsnori – Telavi – Gombori Pass – Tbilisi. Around 250 km and five to six hours at the wheel, best spread over two days. It is asphalt throughout and economy class is entirely sufficient. Tip: during the September harvest every cellar offers a tasting to everyone in the car. Decide who drives before you arrive — Georgia enforces a very low blood-alcohol limit and checks are frequent in Kakheti at that time of year. A second named driver costs 20 GEL per day.

### 3. Tbilisi – Batumi along the Black Sea

370 km on the E60 through Gori, Khashuri, the new Rikoti expressway, Kutaisi, Samtredia and Kobuleti. Five hours. This is the best road in the country, and it is where business class earns its rate: sound insulation and adaptive cruise control genuinely reduce fatigue over that distance. Tip: leave Tbilisi before 07:00 — an hour later adds about 40 minutes just to reach Khashuri. You do not have to drive back either; a one-way rental starts at 100 GEL.

### 4. Svaneti and Mestia

470 km from Tbilisi to Mestia via Zugdidi, eight to nine hours. It can be done in one push, but an overnight stop in Kutaisi or Zugdidi makes far more sense. The road to Mestia is paved and any category will do. The 45 km stretch on to Ushguli is gravel and is permitted only in the off-road 4x4 category — damage taken there in any other car is not covered by the insurance. Tip: Mestia to Ushguli takes two hours each way, so a 09:00 start is not optional if you want to be back before dark.

### 5. Borjomi – Bakuriani – Vardzia

Tbilisi to Borjomi is 160 km (2.5 h), Borjomi to Bakuriani a 30 km climb of switchbacks (45 min), and Borjomi to Vardzia 100 km through Akhaltsikhe and Aspindza (2 h). This is the one route that works just as well in winter, since Bakuriani is a ski resort. Tip: the Vardzia cave complex closes at 17:00, so treat Akhaltsikhe as a fuel stop on the way out and save Rabati Fortress for the return leg.

### 6. Racha and Ambrolauri

Tbilisi – Khashuri – Zestaponi – Ambrolauri, roughly 330 km and six hours. The last 60 km are narrow asphalt cut into the rock, where passing an oncoming car takes real attention — which is why a crossover beats a saloon here. Tip: past Ambrolauri, towards Shovi and Ghebi, petrol stations effectively disappear. Fill up in Ambrolauri. The Khvanchkara cellars expect you to book ahead.

### 7. Tusheti and the Abano Pass

It is only 70 km from Pshaveli to Omalo, and it takes four to five hours: gravel, one car wide, over a pass at 2,850 m. The Abano Pass is open roughly from June to October, requires an off-road 4x4, prior written agreement with us and carries an additional 500 GEL excess. Tip: there is no fuel station in Tusheti, so go up with a full tank, and set off before noon so the descent does not catch you in the dark.

## Matching the category to the route

- Economy class (75 ₾) — Kakheti, Borjomi, Kvemo Kartli, any intercity asphalt.
- Crossover / SUV (130 ₾) — Kazbegi, Racha, Svaneti as far as Mestia, family trips with luggage.
- Off-road 4x4 (240 ₾) — Ushguli, Tusheti, Shatili, anything unpaved.
- Minivan (200 ₾) — a group of six to eight travelling one route together.

Full specifications are on the fleet page, and rates with extras are in the price list.

## Five practical rules

1. Do not plan more than 300 km a day. On mountain roads your average is 45 km/h, not 90.
2. Refuel at half a tank, not at the warning light.
3. Tyres and wheels are not covered by CDW — treat potholes with respect.
4. Check road status and avalanche warnings before departure, especially around Gudauri.
5. Changing your plan is easy: call us from the contact page and we will swap the category if you decide to add a gravel section.

More on seasonal restrictions and route rules is on the FAQ page.


### Rental car vs taxi in Tbilisi: the actual numbers
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/blog/manqanis-daqiraveba-tu-taqsi/ (2026-04-16)
## Defining the unit of comparison

A taxi has one cost line: the fare. A rental car has three, and only the first one appears on a price list. To compare like with like we use the fully loaded daily cost: daily rate plus fuel plus parking.

### Base assumptions

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Economy class rate, 3–6 days | 75 ₾ / day |
| Economy class rate, 7–29 days | 68 ₾ / day |
| Business class rate, 3–6 days | 210 ₾ / day |
| Fuel (60 km/day in town, hybrid) | 12 ₾ / day |
| Paid parking in the centre | 15 ₾ / day |
| Average Bolt city fare | 11 ₾ |
| Bolt, airport to centre | 30 ₾ each way |
| Airport delivery of the car (3+ days) | 0 ₾ |

On those inputs the fully loaded cost of an economy car is 75 + 12 + 15 = 102 GEL per day. For business class the same figure is 237 GEL.

## The break-even point

The formula is straightforward: N = (daily rate + fuel + parking) ÷ average fare.

Economy class: 102 ÷ 11 ≈ 9 rides per day. Below nine movements a day, taxis are cheaper. Once you include the two airport transfers — which are free with a rental of three days or more — the threshold falls to roughly 7 or 8 rides.

Business class: 237 ÷ 20 (comfort-tier fare) ≈ 12 rides per day, which in practice only happens on a delegation schedule.

## Three scenarios, costed

| Scenario | Taxi | Rental | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 days, 5 movements per day | 225 ₾ | 306 ₾ | +81 ₾ against the rental |
| 5 days, 8 movements plus one regional day | 592 ₾ | 538 ₾ | −54 ₾ in favour of the rental |
| 7 days, 8 movements per day | 676 ₾ | 665 ₾ | −11 ₾, effectively a tie |

Scenario 1 — short, city-centre visit. 3 × 5 × 11 = 165 GEL in town plus 60 GEL for airport transfers, so 225 GEL. The rental: 3 × 75 = 225, plus 36 fuel and 45 parking, so 306 GEL. Taxi wins.

Scenario 2 — an intensive week with a regional day. Four city days at eight movements come to 352 GEL, a day out to Rustavi and Mtskheta by taxi costs about 180 GEL, and airport transfers add 60 GEL: 592 GEL in total. The rental: 5 × 75 = 375, fuel over 440 km is 88, parking is 75 — 538 GEL. Rental wins.

Scenario 3 — a full week. From day seven the rate drops to 68 GEL and the two options land within a rounding error of each other. At that point the decision is no longer about price but about time.

## The cost of waiting — the line item nobody budgets

Average wait from ordering to pick-up in Tbilisi runs 5 to 7 minutes, and longer at peak. Eight movements a day therefore consume roughly 45 to 50 minutes of working time.

If a manager's fully loaded cost to the company is 120 GEL an hour, that is 90 to 100 GEL a day of lost capacity. The 81 GEL advantage the taxi held in Scenario 1 disappears on that single line. This is precisely why companies keep choosing a car even when the spreadsheet shows taxis marginally ahead.

## What neither column shows

On the rental side:

- The deposit — 300 GEL on economy, 1,000 GEL on business class. It is blocked on the card rather than charged, and released within 3 business days of return. Treat it as a temporary use of working capital, not as an expense.
- The excess — maximum exposure on damage is 300 to 1,200 GEL depending on category. SCDW takes it to zero for 25–45 GEL per day.
- Traffic fines — at the renter's expense, plus 20 GEL processing, and they can arrive up to 30 days later.
- Late return — free up to 2 hours, then one third of the daily rate for every 3 hours started.

On the taxi side:

- surge pricing that lifts the average fare by 20–40% at exactly the moment you are late for a meeting;
- unpredictable cost for any trip outside the city;
- dozens of small receipts at month end, each one a separate line in an expense report.

That last point is often decisive for a finance team. With a rental you get one contract and one VAT invoice. Companies can pay by bank transfer, and on a corporate contract you receive a single monthly invoice plus a cost report broken down by vehicle.

## When each option wins

Take taxis when:

- the visit is one or two days and stays inside the centre;
- you have fewer than five movements a day;
- the evening involves alcohol;
- parking at the hotel is unavailable or expensive.

Rent a car when:

- the visit runs longer than three days on a dense schedule;
- the plan includes Rustavi, Mtskheta, Kutaisi or a plant visit in the regions;
- you travel as a group of three or four with luggage or demo equipment;
- you need a predictable, pre-approved budget line;
- movements happen after 22:00 or before 06:00.

A third option: a car with a driver, at 120 GEL per day for 8 hours on top of the business class, minivan or 4x4 rate. It is the most expensive column on paper, it reduces lost time to zero, and for a visiting delegation it is frequently the only defensible choice.

## One rule worth stating plainly

Commercial use of a rental car — taxi work, Bolt, courier runs or haulage — is prohibited without prior written consent and voids the insurance cover. It is a common question and the answer is not negotiable.

The full rate table is on the pricing page, the categories on the fleet page and the corporate conditions in the terms. For an exact calculation against your own itinerary, write to us from the contact page — you will have an answer within 15 minutes during business hours.


### How to rent a car in Georgia: a step-by-step guide
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/blog/rogor-viqiravot-manqana-saqartveloshi/ (2026-03-05)
## Step 1. Choose the category and the length

Pick the route first and the car second. For asphalt, economy class from 75 GEL a day is plenty; for mountain routes a crossover from 130 GEL; for gravel — Ushguli, Tusheti — only the off-road 4x4 from 240 GEL is permitted. A minivan for seven or eight starts at 200 GEL, a commercial van at 185 GEL.

Length moves the price directly: from 7 days −10%, from 30 days −25%. A seasonal coefficient of +15% applies in July and August, and +10% over the Easter and New Year weeks. The complete table is on the pricing page.

## Step 2. Book

The site has no online payment module — booking is by phone or email and requires no prepayment. We need your dates, the category, the pickup point and your age, since age affects the rate.

Cancellation terms: more than 48 hours ahead is free; 24 to 48 hours ahead costs one day's rate; less than 24 hours or a no-show costs two days' rate. Changing the dates is free if the car is available.

## Step 3. Documents

| Who you are | Identity | Driving licence | Additional |
|---|---|---|---|
| Georgian citizen | ID card | National, held 2+ years | Card for the deposit |
| Foreign national, Latin alphabet | Passport | National licence | Card for the deposit |
| Foreign national, non-Latin alphabet | Passport | National plus IDP | Card for the deposit |
| Company | Extract from the register | Driver's licence | Power of attorney, stamp |

An International Driving Permit is needed only if your national licence is not issued in the Latin alphabet — an Arabic, Chinese or Japanese licence, for instance. Licences from the EU, the USA, the United Kingdom, Israel and the CIS countries are valid in Georgia as they are. Note too that an IDP is never a standalone document: it is only valid alongside the national licence it translates.

## Step 4. Age and experience

| Category | Minimum age | Experience | Young driver surcharge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Economy class | 21 | 2 years | — |
| Crossover / SUV | 23 | 3 years | 15 ₾ (ages 23–25) |
| Minivan | 23 | 3 years | 15 ₾ (ages 23–25) |
| Business class | 25 | 5 years | 25 ₾ (ages 25–27) |
| Off-road 4x4 | 25 | 4 years | 25 ₾ (ages 25–27) |
| Commercial van | 25 | 3 years | — |

There is no upper age limit. A second driver costs 20 GEL per day, up to two in total; each must meet the same requirements and sign the agreement.

## Step 5. The deposit — how the card block works

This is where most misunderstandings happen. The money is blocked on your card, not charged to it. The bank places an authorisation hold: the amount disappears from your available limit but never leaves your account.

- Economy 300 ₾, crossover 600 ₾, business class and minivan 1,000 ₾, commercial van 800 ₾, off-road 4x4 1,200 ₾.
- The hold is released within 3 business days of the car being returned, provided there is no damage and no fine.
- On a credit card the block eats into your limit; on a debit card it freezes real money. Budget for that on a longer trip.
- If you pay in cash, the deposit is taken in cash and handed back on the spot.

## Step 6. Insurance and the excess

The rate includes CDW (damage to the vehicle) and TPL (third-party liability). CDW caps your liability at the excess: 300 GEL on economy class, up to 1,200 GEL on a 4x4. Even in a serious incident your exposure does not exceed that figure. SCDW at 25–45 GEL per day takes the excess to zero — on a 4x4 down to 300 GEL.

The insurance does not cover: driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs; driving by anyone not named in the agreement; damage taken on unpaved roads unless the car is a 4x4; tyres, wheels, the underbody and the interior; lost keys (400–1,200 GEL); and any commercial use.

## Step 7. Handover and the photo protocol

At handover we complete a report with photographs: all four sides, the interior, the odometer and the fuel level. The identical procedure runs on return, and it is what removes any argument about damage.

While you inspect the car, check for yourself:

1. that every existing scratch is recorded — ask for an extra photo if you are unsure;
2. the windscreen for chips and cracks;
3. tyre condition, plus the spare wheel, jack and wheel brace;
4. the fuel type, petrol or diesel — misfuelling is not covered by the insurance;
5. the vehicle registration document and insurance policy in the glovebox;
6. in winter, the snow chains (20 ₾ per rental, free on a 4x4).

## Step 8. Cross-border travel

| Country | Status | Cost | Daily limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Armenia | Permitted | 150 ₾ | 300 km |
| Turkey | Permitted (selected categories) | 250 ₾ | 300 km |
| Azerbaijan | Prohibited | — | — |
| Russia | Prohibited | — | — |

Permission has to be arranged at least 48 hours in advance, because an international insurance policy and a power of attorney must be prepared. Crossing without permission breaches the agreement and forfeits the entire deposit.

## Step 9. Returning the car

Fuel runs full to full: you receive a full tank and return a full tank. A short tank costs the price of the fuel plus a 20 GEL service fee. Late return is free for up to 2 hours, then one third of the daily rate for every 3 hours started. Returning in another city is possible: Tbilisi↔Kutaisi↔Batumi from 100 GEL.

## Eight mistakes visitors make

1. Arriving without an IDP when one is required. A non-Latin licence with no IDP is grounds for refusing the rental.
2. Ignoring the card limit. A 1,200 GEL hold on a 4x4 takes a real bite out of a travel budget.
3. Taking an economy car onto gravel. Damage on the way to Ushguli or Omalo is not covered — that is an explicit clause, not a technicality.
4. Rushing the inspection. Five minutes of photographs is two hundred times cheaper than a dispute at the return.
5. Forgetting about fines. They can arrive up to 30 days later and are charged with a 20 GEL processing fee.
6. Planning 500 km in a day. Your mountain average is 45 km/h, not 90.
7. Not refuelling before the return. The last station before the airport is not always open.
8. Arranging a border crossing too late. The 48 hours is a technical minimum, not a formality.

The full conditions are on the terms page, remaining questions in the FAQ, and background on the company in about us. To book, call or write from the contact page.


### Driving in Georgia in winter: what you need to know
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/blog/zamtris-mgzavroba-saqartveloshi/ (2026-01-22)
## Winter tyres — the rule and the dates

From 1 December to 1 April every car in the Archi Rent fleet runs on winter tyres, and that is included in the rate — there is nothing to order and nothing extra to pay. Georgian rules require appropriate winter equipment on mountain routes during the cold season, so we simply meet that requirement by default across the fleet.

One practical point people forget: winter tyres are not magic on ice. They shorten your braking distance, but at 60 km/h on a frozen hairpin nothing will save you. In the mountains, double the following distance you would normally keep.

## Snow chains

Chains are separate equipment, and on the Gudauri or Bakuriani runs you will genuinely be glad to have them.

| Equipment | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Winter tyres | 0 ₾ | 1 December – 1 April, included in the rate |
| Snow chains | 20 ₾ per rental | Free on the 4x4 category |
| Roof rack (for skis) | 25 ₾ per day | SUV and 4x4 only |
| Tyre replacement after damage | 120–400 ₾ | Not covered by insurance |

Learn to fit the chains before you leave, in a dry car park, rather than at -8°C halfway up a pass. We will walk you through it in two minutes at our office on Vazha-Pshavela Avenue.

## Which roads actually work in winter

| Route | Winter status | Category |
|---|---|---|
| Tbilisi – Batumi (E60) | Open all year | Economy and up |
| Tbilisi – Kazbegi | Open, Gudauri section closes periodically | Crossover |
| Borjomi – Bakuriani | Open, peak season | Crossover plus chains |
| Zugdidi – Mestia | Usually open, closes briefly after heavy snow | 4x4 |
| Mestia – Ushguli | Effectively impassable | Not rented for this route |
| Abano Pass (Tusheti) | Closed from November to May | — |
| Goderdzi Pass | Frequently closed during blizzards | 4x4 |

Gudauri and the Jvari Pass are the main winter variable. The Georgian Military Road runs through avalanche terrain, and the roads department closes it pre-emptively — sometimes for a few hours, sometimes for a whole day, in both directions. This is not a breakdown and not something we can override: you simply wait.

What that means for planning: a same-day return trip to Kazbegi in winter is a bad idea. If you stay overnight in Stepantsminda and the road shuts, you come back to Tbilisi a day later. If you have a flight that evening, the risk is real. Build the drive so that you return one day before you fly.

## Fuel and daylight

In December the sun sets in Tbilisi around 17:20, and in a mountain valley it goes dark noticeably earlier. That gives you a useful driving window of roughly 08:30 to 16:30 — eight hours, not twelve. Mountain switchbacks, darkness and black ice together are a combination we never recommend to a visiting driver.

- Refuel at half a tank rather than at the warning light. Sitting in a queue behind a closure burns fuel.
- Petrol stations in Kazbegi, Omalo, Ushguli and Shovi are either absent or unreliable.
- Beyond Zhinvali and Pasanauri the stations thin out quickly.
- Keep a phone charger and a blanket in the car. If the road closes, you may be waiting two hours with the engine off.

## Emergency numbers

- 112 — Georgia's single emergency number: police, ambulance, fire and rescue. Operators speak English.
- The Archi Rent hotline — 24/7. If the fault is technical and not caused by the renter, a replacement car reaches you within 6 hours at no charge.

After an accident the order is: 1) call 112; 2) call us; 3) do not leave the scene until the report has been drawn up. Leaving without a police report means losing the insurance cover.

## What the insurance does and does not cover in winter

The CDW included in the price covers damage to the vehicle above the excess (300 ₾ on economy, 1,200 ₾ on a 4x4). But the damage that actually happens in winter tends to land on exactly the parts that are not covered:

- tyres and wheels;
- the underbody;
- mirrors and the interior;
- any damage taken on an unpaved road unless the car is in the 4x4 category.

Sliding a wheel into a kerb on an icy street is the classic winter incident, and it is entirely at the renter's expense. That is why adding SCDW at 25–45 GEL per day pays off more often in winter than in summer — the rates by category are on the pricing page.

## What our winter policy covers

1. Winter tyres on every car from 1 December to 1 April, included in the rate.
2. Chains at 20 GEL per rental, free on 4x4s.
3. 24/7 roadside assistance nationwide.
4. A replacement car within 6 hours for a technical fault.
5. Free date changes when the car is available on the new dates — which matters directly when Gudauri closes.
6. An average fleet age of 4 years with servicing every 8,000 km. In winter that is a battery and brakes question, not a comfort question.

## In short

Winter driving in Georgia is entirely normal if you keep three rules: move through the mountains in daylight, stay above half a tank, and give any mountain day trip a spare day behind it. We handle the rest.

Categories and specifications are on the fleet page, the full conditions on the terms page, and anything left over in the FAQ or straight through contact.



## Road trips

### Georgian Military Highway and Kazbegi
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/military-highway-kazbegi/
2 days / 1 nights | 340 km | 6:40 driving | car: suv | season: all | difficulty: moderate
Stops: Jvari Monastery, Zhinvali Reservoir, Ananuri Fortress, Gudauri and the Russia–Georgia Friendship Monument, Gergeti Trinity Church, Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti Waterfalls
The Georgian Military Highway is the country's most famous mountain road: 155 kilometres from Tbilisi to Stepantsminda, following first the Aragvi and then the Tergi valley and crossing the Jvari Pass at 2,379 metres. Two days is exactly the right amount of time to drive it without rushing — you head north on the first day and drift back on the second, picking up the stops you skipped on the way up.

The scenery changes character several times. First Mtskheta and Jvari Monastery on their confluence hill, then the turquoise water of the Zhinvali reservoir and Ananuri Fortress standing on its headland — the first real stop. After that come the narrow Aragvi gorge, Pasanauri, and the switchbacks up to Gudauri, where the Friendship Monument looks straight into the Devdoraki valley. Beyond the pass the landscape shifts again: rust-orange mineral travertines near Kobi, the tight Tergi defile, and finally Stepantsminda under Gergeti Trinity Church and the 5,047-metre summit of Mount Kazbek.

This route suits travellers who are short on time but want genuine high mountains. It works for families too, because the asphalt runs all the way. The highway is open year round, though in winter the pass closes for a few hours or days after heavy snow, and the last climb to Gergeti needs real ground clearance. Pick a car with enough clearance from our fleet before you set off.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Stepantsminda (170 km, 3 h 30 min)
- 09:00 Leave Tbilisi; after 25 km stop in Mtskheta and at Jvari Monastery (1 h).
- 11:00 Zhinvali reservoir viewpoint, photo stop (30 min).
- 11:45 Ananuri Fortress — the church, the carved facade and the tower (1 h 15 min).
- 13:30 Lunch in Pasanauri or Kvesheti (1 h).
- 15:30 Gudauri and the Friendship Monument (1 h); refuel here if needed.
- 18:00 Arrive Stepantsminda; overnight in Stepantsminda.

Day 2 · Stepantsminda → Tbilisi (170 km, 3 h 10 min)
- 08:30 Climb to Gergeti Trinity Church — 6 km of steep track or a 1.5 h walk (2 h).
- 11:00 Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti waterfalls (1 h 30 min).
- 13:00 Lunch in Stepantsminda (1 h).
- 14:30 Drive back over the pass, stopping at the Kobi travertines (30 min).
- 17:00 Final break at Ananuri or Zhinvali (30 min).
- 19:00 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: Fill up in Pasanauri or Gudauri — petrol stations thin out beyond the pass. In winter the Jvari Pass can close for hours or days after snowfall; check road status before leaving. The track up to Gergeti is narrow and steep — high clearance and dry weather are essential. Monasteries have a dress code: headscarf and long skirt for women, long trousers for men. It is 15-20°C colder in the mountains than in Tbilisi; bring a jacket even in July. Book your Stepantsminda hotel in advance, especially in July and August.

### Kakheti Wine Loop
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/kakheti-wine-loop/
3 days / 2 nights | 420 km | 8:00 driving | car: economy | season: all | difficulty: easy
Stops: Sighnaghi, Bodbe Monastery, Telavi and Batonis Tsikhe, Tsinandali Estate, Alaverdi Cathedral, Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone
Kakheti is the heart of Georgian wine and the easiest region in the country to drive. The whole loop is on asphalt, the legs between stops are short, and you are never more than two hours from Tbilisi. Three days is what it takes to stop rushing through cellars and instead sit down, taste properly and sleep where you tasted.

Day one belongs to Sighnaghi, the walled hill town whose cobbled lanes and rampart walk frame the Alazani valley and the whole Caucasus ridge in a single view; two kilometres away is Bodbe Monastery, the burial place of St Nino. Day two is the regional capital, Telavi, with the Batonis Tsikhe palace of King Erekle II, followed by Tsinandali — the Chavchavadze estate with its English-style garden and the 1841 cellar that produced Georgia's first bottled wine. Day three opens with Alaverdi, a fifty-metre eleventh-century cathedral standing alone in the fields, and ends in the Kindzmarauli zone around Kvareli.

What you actually see: qvevri cellars where wine ferments in buried clay jars, family tables that turn into long lunches, endless vineyards under the mountains, and several of the greatest monuments of Georgian architecture. The route works all year, but late September and October, during the rtveli harvest, is unbeatable. An economy car is entirely enough. One rule matters above all: whoever drives does not taste.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Sighnaghi (115 km, 2 h)
- 09:30 Leave Tbilisi on the Kakheti highway, coffee stop near Sagarejo.
- 11:30 Arrive Sighnaghi and check in.
- 12:30 Lunch, then the cobbled centre, the town wall and the valley view (2 h).
- 15:30 Bodbe Monastery and the spring of St Nino (1 h 30 min).
- 18:00 Tasting at a family cellar in Sighnaghi or Bodbe.
- Overnight in Sighnaghi.

Day 2 · Sighnaghi → Telavi (60 km, 1 h 15 min)
- 10:00 Drive via Tsnori and Gurjaani with views over the Alazani valley.
- 11:30 Telavi: Batonis Tsikhe, the royal palace and the 900-year-old plane tree (2 h).
- 14:00 Lunch near the Telavi market (1 h).
- 16:00 The two Shuamta monasteries or a walk through town (1 h 30 min).
- 19:00 Dinner with a tasting; overnight in Telavi.

Day 3 · Telavi → Tsinandali → Alaverdi → Kvareli → Tbilisi (215 km, 4 h 15 min)
- 09:00 Tsinandali estate, garden and historic cellar (2 h).
- 11:30 Alaverdi Cathedral (1 h).
- 13:30 Kvareli: the Kindzmarauli winery and the wine tunnels (2 h).
- 15:30 Late lunch in Kvareli or by Ilia Lake (1 h).
- 17:00 Return via Gurjaani and Sagarejo.
- 20:00 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: The driver does not taste — Georgia enforces a zero alcohol limit; agree in advance who drives each day. The rtveli harvest runs from late September through October: the best time for cellars, and the time hotels fill first. Call small family cellars ahead — many receive guests by appointment only. Alaverdi and Bodbe have a dress code; scarves and wraps are usually available at the gate. Leave boot space for bottles, and pack them upright and padded for the drive home.

### Vardzia and Borjomi — the Southern Route
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/vardzia-borjomi-south/
2 days / 1 nights | 550 km | 9:00 driving | car: economy | season: all | difficulty: moderate
Stops: Borjomi Central Park and Mineral Springs, Rabati Castle (Akhaltsikhe), Khertvisi Fortress, Vardzia
This is the southern direction — the Mtkvari valley, which leads out of Tbilisi through Borjomi and Akhaltsikhe and ends close to the Turkish border at the rock-cut city of Vardzia. All 265 kilometres are asphalt, so an economy car reaches the end comfortably, although the final stretch narrows and winds along the gorge.

Day one is the climb from the plain into the mountains. Borjomi is a nineteenth-century spa town where you drink the famous mineral water straight from the spring in the central park. Then the valley tightens and Akhaltsikhe appears with Rabati Castle, a rebuilt citadel that holds a mosque, a church, a synagogue and the old fortress towers inside a single wall. Day two continues south: Khertvisi Fortress guards the confluence of two rivers, and then comes Vardzia itself — a twelfth-century monastery carved into the cliff under Queen Tamar, thirteen storeys deep, with hundreds of chambers and the frescoed Church of the Dormition at its heart.

The route suits travellers who care about history and architecture: in two days you cover two millennia. Respect the distances, though — you spend over four hours a day behind the wheel, so the overnight in Akhaltsikhe or near Vardzia is not optional. Doing it as a day trip means 530 kilometres in one go. The road stays open in winter, but the Javakheti plateau is genuinely cold.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Borjomi → Akhaltsikhe (205 km, 3 h 20 min)
- 08:30 Leave Tbilisi on the E60 via Gori and Khashuri.
- 11:00 Borjomi Central Park, the mineral spring and the cable car (2 h).
- 13:30 Lunch in Borjomi (1 h).
- 15:00 The Mtkvari gorge towards Akhaltsikhe, stop at Atskuri (30 min).
- 16:30 Rabati Castle in Akhaltsikhe — upper citadel, mosque and museum (2 h).
- Overnight in Akhaltsikhe.

Day 2 · Akhaltsikhe → Vardzia → Tbilisi (345 km, 5 h 40 min)
- 09:00 Set off towards Aspindza along the river.
- 10:00 Khertvisi Fortress at the confluence (45 min).
- 11:15 Vardzia — the cave city, the church and its frescoes (2 h 30 min).
- 14:00 Lunch near Vardzia or in Aspindza (1 h).
- 15:30 Drive back via Akhaltsikhe and Borjomi.
- 21:00 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: Fill the tank in Akhaltsikhe — stations are rare beyond Aspindza. Vardzia means many stairs and narrow tunnels: wear proper shoes and bring a small torch. In summer Vardzia bakes in full sun — go early morning or after 16:00, with water and a hat. The Javakheti plateau is cold eight months a year; winter tyres are mandatory in the cold season. Vardzia and back in one day is 530 km — the overnight in Akhaltsikhe makes the trip far more pleasant.

### Imereti: Caves and Canyons
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/imereti-caves-canyons/
3 days / 2 nights | 640 km | 10:30 driving | car: suv | season: may-october | difficulty: moderate
Stops: Uplistsikhe, Bagrati Cathedral and central Kutaisi, Motsameta Monastery, Gelati Monastery, Sataplia Nature Reserve, Prometheus Cave, Okatse Canyon, Kinchkha Waterfall
Imereti is the limestone corner of Georgia, and limestone means caves, canyons and waterfalls. Kutaisi, the country's second city, is the perfect base for all of it: nothing on this route is more than an hour's drive from the centre. Three days is the honest minimum, because this density of natural and historical sights simply does not compress into one.

The first stop on the way west is Uplistsikhe, the rock-cut town near Gori where pagan sacrificial halls and Hellenistic chambers survive above the Mtkvari. In Kutaisi you get Bagrati Cathedral on its hill and one of the liveliest markets in the country, and just outside town stand Gelati, the UNESCO-listed academy founded by David the Builder with its great apse mosaic, and tiny Motsameta perched over a river bend. Day two goes underground: the stalactite halls and subterranean river of Prometheus Cave, then Sataplia with its fossilised dinosaur footprints and glass viewing platform. Day three is the Okatse canyon walkway, 700 metres of steel path bolted to the cliff, and the Kinchkha waterfall.

One warning: the approach to Okatse and Kinchkha turns to gravel after Gordi and does not forgive rain, so decent ground clearance genuinely matters here. The season runs May to October — the canyons often close in winter, while the caves stay open all year.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Uplistsikhe → Kutaisi (245 km, 4 h)
- 08:30 Leave Tbilisi on the E60.
- 10:00 Uplistsikhe — the cave town and its museum (2 h).
- 12:30 Lunch in Gori (1 h).
- 16:00 Arrive Kutaisi: Bagrati Cathedral and the Rioni embankment (1 h 30 min).
- 19:00 Dinner in the centre; overnight in Kutaisi.

Day 2 · Gelati, Prometheus and Sataplia (90 km, 2 h)
- 09:00 Motsameta Monastery on its rock spur (45 min).
- 10:15 Gelati Monastery — mosaic, academy, tomb of King David (1 h 30 min).
- 13:00 Lunch in Tskaltubo or Kutaisi (1 h).
- 14:30 Prometheus Cave, guided walk and the underground boat ride (2 h).
- 17:00 Sataplia Reserve: dinosaur footprints and the glass platform (1 h 30 min).
- Overnight in Kutaisi.

Day 3 · Okatse, Kinchkha → Tbilisi (305 km, 4 h 30 min)
- 08:30 Drive to Gordi; the last 6 km are gravel.
- 09:45 Okatse Canyon — the hanging walkway and viewpoint (2 h).
- 12:15 Kinchkha waterfall (1 h).
- 13:30 Lunch in Gordi or Khoni (1 h).
- 15:00 Return via Zestafoni and the Rikoti pass.
- 20:00 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: The final kilometres to Okatse and Kinchkha are gravel — high clearance is needed, doubly so after rain. Prometheus Cave holds 14°C year round: bring a jacket and non-slip shoes. Cave visits run in guided groups with tickets sold on site; midday queues are the longest. Gelati and Motsameta enforce a dress code — headscarf and covered shoulders. Staying in Kutaisi is far cheaper than near the canyons, and everything is 40-60 minutes away. Fill up in Kutaisi — there is no station on the road towards Gordi.

### Svaneti Expedition
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/svaneti-expedition/
5 days / 4 nights | 1050 km | 21:00 driving | car: offroad | season: june-september | difficulty: hard
Stops: Bagrati Cathedral and central Kutaisi, Dadiani Palace, Zugdidi, Enguri Dam and Jvari Reservoir, Mestia and the Svan Towers, Chalaadi Glacier, Ushguli
Upper Svaneti is the most remote and the most memorable corner of Georgia. Tbilisi to Mestia is 470 kilometres and eight and a half hours — a full day behind the wheel — which is why this route is built around five days: two on the road, three in the mountains. Rushing it makes no sense.

The drive changes character as you go. First Kutaisi and the Colchis lowland, then Zugdidi with the Dadiani palace, then the Enguri Dam, a 271-metre arch wall with a turquoise reservoir behind it. From the dam the Enguri gorge begins and climbs for seventy kilometres, narrowing until the stone towers of Mestia appear. From Mestia nothing is far: the Chalaadi glacier is a ninety-minute walk from the road bridge, the Hatsvali cable car opens a full panorama of Ushba, and Ushguli is 45 kilometres and roughly two hours away — one of the highest permanently inhabited villages in Europe, under the wall of Shkhara.

This trip demands preparation. The Mestia-Ushguli road is partly gravel and crosses shallow fords that rise with the meltwater, so a genuine four-wheel-drive vehicle is not a suggestion. The season runs June to September; from October the passes start catching snow. Conditions for off-road vehicles are set out on our pricing page.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Kutaisi → Zugdidi (320 km, 4 h 50 min)
- 08:00 Leave Tbilisi on the E60.
- 11:30 Kutaisi: Bagrati Cathedral and lunch (2 h).
- 15:30 Zugdidi, the Dadiani Palace and its botanical garden (1 h 30 min).
- Overnight in Zugdidi.

Day 2 · Zugdidi → Enguri → Mestia (150 km, 3 h 20 min)
- 09:00 Set off towards Jvari.
- 09:45 Enguri Dam and the reservoir viewpoint (1 h).
- 11:00 Up the Enguri gorge; stop and lunch at Khaishi (1 h).
- 15:00 Arrive Mestia: Svan towers and the museum (2 h).
- Overnight in Mestia.

Day 3 · Mestia and Chalaadi (30 km, 1 h)
- 09:00 Drive to the Chalaadi bridge, then a 1 h 30 min walk to the glacier.
- 13:00 Lunch in Mestia (1 h).
- 15:00 Hatsvali cable car and the Ushba panorama (2 h 30 min).
- Overnight in Mestia.

Day 4 · Mestia → Ushguli → Mestia (90 km, 4 h)
- 08:30 Leave for Ushguli — gravel sections and fords.
- 10:30 Ushguli — the towers of Chazhashi and Lamaria church (2 h).
- 13:00 Lunch in Ushguli with the Shkhara view (1 h 30 min).
- 16:00 Drive back through Ipari and Kala.
- Overnight in Mestia.

Day 5 · Mestia → Tbilisi (470 km, 8 h 30 min)
- 07:30 Early start down the Enguri gorge.
- 11:00 Zugdidi: coffee and fuel (45 min).
- 13:30 Lunch in Kutaisi or Samtredia (1 h).
- 18:00 Break at the Rikoti pass (30 min).
- 20:30 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: The Mestia-Ushguli section is gravel with river fords — 4x4 only, about two hours each way. The season is June to September; in May and October snow can close the Ushguli road without warning. Refuel in Zugdidi and in Mestia — there is almost nothing in between. Mobile coverage drops out in the gorge; download offline maps before you leave. Mestia beds sell out early in July and August; Ushguli guesthouses are simpler and colder. Mountain weather turns fast — a rain shell and warm layers are needed even in midsummer.

### Black Sea and Adjara
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/black-sea-adjara/
4 days / 3 nights | 880 km | 14:30 driving | car: suv | season: may-october | difficulty: moderate
Stops: Bagrati Cathedral and central Kutaisi, Kobuleti Beach and Protected Areas, Batumi Botanical Garden, Batumi Boulevard and Old Town, Gonio-Apsaros Fortress, Makhuntseti Waterfall and Arched Bridge, Mtirala National Park
Tbilisi to Batumi is 370 kilometres and five and a half hours — a full driving day that is much better broken with a stop in Kutaisi. Four days gives you both halves of Adjara: the coast and the mountains behind it. Batumi is not only a beach; half an hour inland the subtropical forest and the waterfalls begin.

Day one is mostly driving, with Kutaisi as the break. Day two runs along the coast: the long pebble beach of Kobuleti, the Batumi Botanical Garden on Green Cape with its Japanese, Himalayan and Mediterranean sections spilling down to the sea, and finally Batumi itself — the boulevard, the old town and the lit-up towers at night. Day three heads south to Gonio-Apsaros Fortress, a Roman castellum where, by tradition, the Apostle Matthias is buried. Day four goes up into the hills: the Adjaristsqali valley, the arched stone bridge and waterfall at Makhuntseti, then Mtirala National Park, the wettest place in Georgia.

Take the climate seriously: Adjara receives up to 2,500 millimetres of rain a year and summer downpours are common. Some sections inside Mtirala and up the valley need real ground clearance. The swimming season runs June to September, while May and October are excellent for the mountains, the waterfalls and the empty coastal road.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Kutaisi → Batumi (370 km, 5 h 30 min)
- 08:00 Leave Tbilisi on the E60.
- 11:30 Kutaisi: Bagrati Cathedral and lunch (2 h).
- 17:00 Arrive Batumi, check in, evening on the boulevard (2 h).
- Overnight in Batumi.

Day 2 · Kobuleti and the Botanical Garden (90 km, 1 h 30 min)
- 09:30 Drive north to Kobuleti for the beach and promenade (2 h 30 min).
- 13:00 Lunch in Kobuleti (1 h).
- 15:00 Batumi Botanical Garden on Green Cape (2 h 30 min).
- 19:00 Batumi old town and Piazza (1 h 30 min).
- Overnight in Batumi.

Day 3 · Gonio and Batumi (40 km, 1 h)
- 10:00 Gonio-Apsaros Fortress and its museum (1 h 30 min).
- 12:00 Beach time at Gonio or Kvariati (2 h).
- 15:00 Late lunch at a seafront restaurant (1 h 30 min).
- 18:00 Batumi cable car and the Alphabet Tower (2 h).
- Overnight in Batumi.

Day 4 · Makhuntseti, Mtirala → Tbilisi (400 km, 6 h 30 min)
- 08:00 Up the Adjaristsqali valley to the Makhuntseti bridge and waterfall (1 h 30 min).
- 10:30 Mtirala National Park, short trail and suspension bridge (2 h).
- 13:00 Lunch in Chakvi or Kobuleti (1 h).
- 14:30 Drive back via Samtredia and Kutaisi.
- 21:00 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: It rains often in Adjara — pack a waterproof and a spare pair of shoes even in summer. The park road inside Mtirala and parts of the valley need proper ground clearance. Parking in Batumi is expensive and scarce in summer; choose a hotel with its own parking. The beaches are pebble, not sand (except Ureki) — water shoes make a real difference. Coastal prices double in July and August; May, June and September are calmer and cheaper. Tbilisi-Batumi is 5 h 30 min in one go — plan an early start on day one.

### Racha Mountain Loop
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/routes/racha-mountain-loop/
3 days / 2 nights | 790 km | 14:00 driving | car: suv | season: may-october | difficulty: moderate
Stops: Bagrati Cathedral and central Kutaisi, Nikortsminda Cathedral, Shaori Reservoir, Shovi Resort
Racha is the quietest mountain region in Georgia — no crowds, no large hotels, but forest, lakes, stone villages and the vineyards that produce Khvanchkara. The route climbs from Kutaisi through Tkibuli and over the Nakerala pass, runs on to Ambrolauri and Oni, and ends in the alpine valley of Shovi.

The first day is long: 230 kilometres to Kutaisi, then the Tkibuli reservoir and the switchbacks of Nakerala, where the Racha ranges open up for the first time. Just beyond the pass stands Nikortsminda, an eleventh-century cathedral with what is probably the richest carved facade in the country, almost entirely covered in relief work. Then comes Shaori reservoir, set in pine forest at 1,100 metres, where locals swim in high summer. Day two follows the Rioni upstream from Ambrolauri through Oni to Shovi, where the valley narrows and the road climbs into subalpine meadows below the main Caucasus ridge.

Racha suits travellers who want silence and landscape and do not need polished tourist infrastructure. The road is paved as far as Ambrolauri, though narrow and winding on the pass, and the surface deteriorates past Oni — ground clearance helps here. The season is May to October; in winter Nakerala catches snow and can close for days.
Day 1 · Tbilisi → Kutaisi → Nikortsminda → Ambrolauri (335 km, 5 h 30 min)
- 08:00 Leave Tbilisi on the E60, break at the Rikoti pass.
- 11:30 Kutaisi: lunch and a short walk (1 h 30 min).
- 14:00 Tkibuli reservoir and the Nakerala pass viewpoint (45 min).
- 15:30 Nikortsminda Cathedral — carvings and cupola (1 h).
- 17:30 Arrive Ambrolauri; wine house and a Khvanchkara tasting (1 h).
- Overnight in Ambrolauri.

Day 2 · Shaori, Oni and Shovi (150 km, 3 h)
- 09:00 Shaori reservoir in the pine forest, walk along the shore (1 h 30 min).
- 11:30 The Rioni valley towards Oni, stop at Barakoni church (45 min).
- 13:00 Oni: the old centre and lunch (1 h 30 min).
- 15:30 The alpine valley of Shovi and its mineral springs (2 h).
- 19:00 Drive back; overnight in Ambrolauri or Oni.

Day 3 · Ambrolauri → Tbilisi (330 km, 5 h 30 min)
- 09:00 Market and last purchases in Ambrolauri (1 h).
- 10:30 Return over Nakerala and through Tkibuli.
- 13:00 Lunch in Kutaisi (1 h 30 min).
- 15:00 East on the E60 via Zestafoni and Khashuri.
- 19:30 Back in Tbilisi.
Tips: The Nakerala pass is narrow and winding — take it slowly in fog, and expect worse surface beyond Oni. Fill up in Kutaisi and Ambrolauri; between Oni and Shovi there is almost nothing. Accommodation in Racha is limited and mostly family-run — book your nights in advance. Genuine Khvanchkara comes only from the Ambrolauri zone; check the label and producer before buying. In winter Nakerala catches snow and can close for days; May to October is far safer. ATMs are scarce around Oni and Shovi — take cash with you.


## Regions

### Tbilisi
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/regions/tbilisi/
Tbilisi sits on both banks of the Mtkvari in a narrow valley, hemmed in by wooded ridges, and that shape explains most of the city. The historic centre is small enough to walk: Narikala Fortress on the ridge above, the brick domes of the Abanotubani sulphur baths in the gorge below, and within a few hundred metres of one another a mosque, a synagogue and an Armenian church.

A second day opens the city up. The Mtatsminda funicular climbs to a park and a terrace high above the rooftops. The Georgian National Museum on Rustaveli holds the gold of the Colchian burials and the permanent exhibition on the Soviet occupation. Holy Trinity Cathedral, huge and modern, stands over Avlabari on the opposite bank. On the green edge of town, Turtle Lake sits beside the Open Air Museum of Ethnography, where timber houses brought from every province are reassembled among the trees, and further north the columns of the Chronicle of Georgia rise above the Tbilisi Sea.

Seasons matter less here than anywhere else in the country, since everything is open year-round. July and August are heavy — the valley traps heat and the afternoons drag — so sightseeing works best early and late in the day. Spring and autumn are the good months. Winter is mild and snow rarely lasts more than a day or two.

Two days cover the centre comfortably, three if you want a bathhouse, a museum and an unhurried evening. Most visitors also treat Tbilisi as a base: Mtskheta is half an hour out, Gori a little over an hour, Kakheti under two. It is both a destination and the place where a Georgian road trip begins and ends.
Driving: Driving in Tbilisi is the least enjoyable part of a Georgian trip. Traffic is dense, lane discipline is loose, minibuses stop wherever a passenger waves, and cars change lanes with little warning. None of it is dangerous at city speeds, but it rewards patience rather than assertion. The urban limit is 50 km/h, speed cameras are common on the main avenues, and the rush hours run roughly 08:30–10:00 and 17:30–19:30.

Parking is the real problem. Street parking in the central districts is zonal and paid, enforced by patrol cameras, and around Abanotubani and the Old Town there is effectively none. Use a paid lot or a shopping-centre garage and walk in. The old lanes are narrow, steep and frequently one-way, so a large car becomes a liability. An economy model handles the city and the highways out of it; see the fleet if the mountains come later.

### Mtskheta-Mtianeti
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/regions/mtskheta-mtianeti/
Mtskheta-Mtianeti starts immediately north of Tbilisi and runs up to the main ridge of the Caucasus. Its southern end is low and historic: Mtskheta, Georgia's first capital, with Svetitskhoveli Cathedral in the middle of town, and above it on a rock spur the Jvari Monastery, looking down on the confluence of the Aragvi and the Mtkvari. Both are UNESCO-listed and both are half an hour from the capital.

North of that begins the Georgian Military Highway, the country's most famous drive. The green water of the Zhinvali Reservoir, the fortified complex of Ananuri on its shore, then a long climb to Gudauri — a ski resort in winter, and in summer the way to the Russia-Georgia Friendship Monument and the Jvari Pass at 2,379 metres. Beyond the watershed lies Kazbegi: the town of Stepantsminda, Gergeti Trinity Church at 2,170 metres against the cone of Mount Kazbek, the Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti waterfalls.

The side valleys are a different world again. Truso opens west of the highway with mineral springs and rust-coloured travertine terraces. In Khevsureti, Shatili is a village built as a single mass of stone towers near the northern border, reached over a high unpaved pass.

Seasonality is sharp. Mtskheta, Ananuri and Zhinvali are open all year; Gudauri runs from December to March for skiing; Truso and Shatili are realistically June to September. Half a day covers Mtskheta, a full day gets you to Kazbegi, and a night in Stepantsminda makes it far better.
Driving: The Military Highway (S3) is paved for its whole length, but it is a mountain road and behaves like one. The stretch between Gudauri and Kobi is avalanche-prone, and in heavy snow the police close it for hours or days at a time; winter tyres are required from November to March and chains are worth carrying. Queues of freight lorries heading for the Dariali border crossing are common and make overtaking awkward on the narrow sections.

The last six kilometres up to Gergeti Trinity are steep and badly broken — you need real ground clearance or one of the local jeeps. Truso and Shatili are unpaved and 4x4 only; the Datvisjvari Pass towards Shatili is usually open from June to October. Fill up in Pasanauri or Gudauri. The classic mistake is attempting Kazbegi as a winter day return and crossing the pass in the dark.

### Kakheti
URL: https://www.example.ge/en/regions/kakheti/
Kakheti is Georgia's wine country and the easiest region in which to spend two unhurried days. The Alazani Valley runs north-east between the Gombori ridge and the wall of the Greater Caucasus, and almost everything worth seeing lies along that axis. Telavi is the practical centre, with Batonis Tsikhe, the residence of King Erekle II, in the middle of town. Sighnaghi, an hour to the south, is a small walled hill town with a long rampart and a view over the whole valley; Bodbe Monastery, the burial place of St Nino, sits just outside it.

The churches are the oldest layer. Alaverdi Cathedral rises above the vineyards in one clean sweep of eleventh-century stone. Ikalto was an academy as much as a monastery. Nekresi looks down from a wooded slope, and Gremi is what survives of a royal capital sacked in 1615. Tsinandali Estate keeps a nineteenth-century house, an English-style park and a cellar, while Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone are the place to work out how the semi-sweet reds are made.

Two extremes bracket the region. In the south-east, David Gareja stands in a bare striped semi-desert, a landscape with nothing in common with the vineyards. In the north, beyond the Abano Pass, Tusheti and the village of Omalo are reachable only in summer and only in a four-wheel drive.
